{"notes": "Visit 1 (2:45). Early stage, so ratings are provisional. I can't tell who placed which domino, so I'm judging only what I saw and heard.

Table state: the top line runs from the start to the tail tip (~28.5, 5.5) and is fully connected. The bottom line is connected but stops at ~(16.5, 13.8), where Tom's hands are, so it still has about 12 units to go. Neither the tail's back edge nor the notch is built yet.

Leo: Acting as coordinator. He gave contradictory instructions twice (tail as strokes 3 and 4, then a single stroke 3 for the back edge with the notch). Maya had already started on the first version, so this cost her some time. He owned the mistakes straight away, and his latest plan is coherent: he lays the back edge himself and Tom carries the bottom line to the tail tip. Watch whether his instructions stay stable. Leadership and collaboration are mixed so far.

Maya: Responsive and clear. She took the task, noticed it didn't match her pad, and told Leo. She sensibly extended off the end of the top line, and the top line is complete. Good communication and execution. She was told to hold off on the back edge.

Priya: Reported the top line finished and connected. She offered Tom help with the bottom line and was checking the body-to-tail joint. Proactive and supportive, and I'd like to see her follow through on the help offer.

Tom: Silent while I was there, and I have no direct evidence of problems. He's making steady progress on the longest remaining stretch, and the bottom line is still connected. He didn't take up Priya's offer. Check whether he's under-communicating or just focused, and whether the bottom line reaches the tail in time."}
